# correlation and regression analysis

### defn: correlation; measure the strength and direction of linear rltship btn  2 var


# correlation analysis
```{r}

dataset<-data.frame(
x=c(1:5),
y=c(2, 4, 5, 7, 6)
)
head(dataset)

```


# pearson correlation 

```{r}
pearson_corr<-cor.test(dataset$x, dataset$y, method="pearson")
print(paste("pearson correlation:",pearson_corr))
```


# There is strong correlation btn x and y



# is association significant?

# test significance of pearson_correlation

# HO: 
# H1:

```{r}
pearson_corr_test<-cor.test(dataset$x, dataset$y, method="pearson")
print(pearson_corr_test)
```


- since the p-value<5%, we reject the null hypontesis nad conclude that hence their exist relation is significant btn x and y



# spearman correlation 

```{r}
spearman_corr<-cor.test(dataset$x, dataset$y, method="spearman")
print(paste("spearman correlation:",pearson_corr))
```

# strong positive correlation

## is the rel;ationship significant?

```{r}
spearman_corr_test<-cor.test(dataset$x, dataset$y, method="spearman")
print(spearman_corr_test)
```
- since te p-value > 5%, we fail to reject the nul hypothesis and conclude that there is no significant difference between x an y valuables





# regression analysis


# defn: regression; rltshp btn independent $ dependent variables

## simple linear regration
```{r}
model<-lm(y~x,data=dataset)
summary(model)
```



- a unit increase in variable x increses variable y by 1.1unit, and effect is significant since the p-value <5%

- var X, explains variabvle y by 81,76% but the remainingpercentage is explained by other factors not in our model


# read data series



# muiltiple linear regression

```{r}
data1<-data.frame(
  y=c(2, 4, 5, 4, 6),
  x1=c(1:5),
  x2=c(3,5, 7, 6, 8)
)
model1<-lm(y~x1+x2, data=data1)
summary(model1)
```


- a unit increase in x1, decreases y by 0.1778
- a unit increase in x2, increases y by 0.8889 


- var X1 and x2, explains variabvle y by  0.9697 but the remainingpercentage is explained by other factors not in our model

# check whether model1 is significance


# model diagnosis

```{r}
par(mfrow<-c(1,2)) # setting up 1 by 1 plot layout

plot(model1)
```



# import data set




```{r}
nck<-read.csv("gsssubset.csv")
head(nck)
```



# Calculate pearson correlartion



```{r}
pearson_test<-cor.test(nck$income, nck$hrswrk, method="pearson")
print(paste("pearson correlation:",pearson_test))
```


# testing significance

```{r}
pearson_test_sign<-cor.test(nck$income, nck$hrswrk, method="pearson")
print(pearson_test_sign)
```

- since the p-value<5%, we  reject null analysis and conclude that there exist  significance between income and hours of work



# select continous var



```{r}
nck_selected<-nck %>% 
   select(hrswrk,age, weight, income, height )
cor(nck_selected)
```

# a correlation matrix

# regression analysis

```{r}
model2<-lm(income~age+height+weight+hrswrk, data=nck)
summary(model2)
```
